sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 01.01.2024.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 01.01.2024 at about 1.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing No.KA-40-X- 3617 from Nandi Hills towards Maligenahalli, Bidalur,while proceeding so, when he reached in front of Gowdru Hotel, Neeleri Nandi Hills road,
he parked the vehicle on edge of the road and stood adjacent to the vehicle, at that time the driver of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 came from behind in the same direction with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Shirdi Sai hospital,
Devanahalli, wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 43 years, being Private employee earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.

3. In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.1- owner has not appeared before the tribunal,
hence, placed exparte.

After service of summons, the respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the existence of policy in respect of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429.
Further it has denied the involvement of the offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 in the alleged accident and contended that, there is a delay in filing the FIR.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident by contending that the alleged accident was due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle towards the cause of accident.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that there is no fitness certificate and permit to the vehicle of the respondent No.1 to ply vehicle on the road at the time of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

sentences.text:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of vehicle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 by its rider,
in RTA took place on 01.01.2024 at about 1.30 p.m. in front of Gowdru Hotel,
Neeleri, Nandi Hills road, Bengaluru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 17.
Further examined the Dr. S.A. Somashekara, Orthopaedic surgeon at Victoria hospital were examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P18 & Ex.P19.
The respondent does not choosen to lead any evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by one Basavaraju who is the police officer at Devanahalli traffic police station by alleging the rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429.
In continuation the IO conducted spot mahazar along with sketch as per Ex.P3 & P.4.
On perusal of Ex.P3 and P.4 the accident spot is in the left side edge of the road.
It is alleged that the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04- KP-7429 came to the extreme edge of the road and dashed against the parked motorcycle in which the petitioner was sitting.
The contents of Ex.P.3 and P.4 shows that the rider of the offending vehicle by riding this vehicle in negligent manner dashed the petitioner's motorcycle.

10. The Ex.P.5 is the IMV report wherein the motor cycle of the petitioner bearing No.
KA.40-X-3617 has got damages in its headlight mask broken, front right side indicator broken, rear Kantharaju vs Roopa on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185298239/
3 right side broken and the offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 has got damages in its headlight assembly, front both side indicator, front number plate bent, both side view mirror broken, steering handle bent.
This shows that the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 was rode the said motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner, as such caused the accident without controlling the said vehicle.
As such the negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 is established.

11. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 and produced documents in support of his case to prove the alleged negligence.
The PW.1 was cross-examined at length by denying the negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 but nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.

Thus, it can be concluded that, the negligence is on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 who caused the accident by riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 in a rash and negligent manner.
12. Ex.P7 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner and also to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.
13. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429.
14.
The respondent No.2 insurance company even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
No rebuttal evidence is placed by either of the respondents.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the driver of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 338 of IPC.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

15. By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04- KP-7429.

sentences.text: In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

18. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
19. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 01.01.2024 which is caused by the driver of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP- 7429 which is belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.

In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
20.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA- 04-KP-7429.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 43 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P12 the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 1980.
The accident was took place on 01.01.2024.
Hence as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 44 years.
The petitioner has produced discharge summaries marked at Ex.P8.

As per Ex.P8 the petitioner was admitted to Sri Shirdi Sai hospital from 01.01.2024 to 08.01.2024 and 11.03.2024 to 13.03.2024,
and has sustained type-II comminuted fracture of both bone right leg, distal 3rd total amputation of right thumb also has also underwent wound debridement and ORIF with LCP- Tibia and fibula  under SA, debridment and stump closure - right thumb under LA on 01.01.2024.
By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.75,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

Kantharaju vs Roopa on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185298239/
5 b) Medical expenses:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced medical bill as per Ex.P10 amounting to Rs.3,34,957/- which are supported by medical prescriptions and advance receipts marked at Ex.P9 & 11.
The medical bill is not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bill.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e.,
Rs. 3,35,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was a Private employee and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has produced has not produced any documents.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered in the year 2024 at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P8 - the petitioner was admitted to Sri Shirdi Sai hospital from 01.01.2024 to 08.01.2024 and 11.03.2024 to 13.03.2024 totally for the period of 11 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 4 months period including 11 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500 X 4 months = Rs.66,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr. S.A.
Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.2 and through him clinical notes and X-rays were got marked at Ex.P18 & 19.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained type-II comminuted fracture of both bone right leg, distal 3rd total amputation of right thumb also has also underwent wound debridement and ORIF with LCP- Tibia and fibula  under SA, debridment and stump closure - right thumb under LA on 01.01.2024.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
The Ex.P13 photographs shows that the right hand thumb of the petitioner is amputated.

In this regard, I rely on the reportable decision, in Civil Appeal No.2476/2019 in the case of M.R.Krishamurthi V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd., decided on 05.03.2019, the Hon'ble supreme court has held as follows, "We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i) All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.

entities.text: M.R.Krishamurthi V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that the percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as the percentage of permanent disability).
Kantharaju vs Roopa on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185298239/
6

entities.text: Kantharaju vs Roopa on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) The doctor who treated an injured claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard to the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv) The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession, occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
The PW.2 doctor who assessed the physical disability of the petitioner stated that the physical disability to lower limb at 40% and to whole body is assessed at 20%.
The loss of right thumb is considered as 25% disability.
There is a non-union of fracture of distal fibula and also amputation of right thumb.

A perusal of the injuries sustained, treatment taken and in view of the citation referred above, it is considered that though the petitioner is having 20% permanent physical whole body disability, his avocational disability is 18%.
Hence considering all these aspects this tribunal has taken disability at 18%.
The petitioner has stated that he was Private employee and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
To consider the avocation of the petitioner except the oral evidence, no documents or proof of salary is shown by the petitioner.
Such being the case it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2024.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '14'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,500/- X 12 X 14 X 18% =Rs.4,98,960/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P8 discharge summary, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 11 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injury sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.35,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES: The petitioner sustained grievous injury in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 11 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.11,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 11 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.

Therefore, it is just Kantharaju vs Roopa on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185298239/
7 and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.45,000/- under this head.

Hence, by looking to the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment taken by him, I inclined to award Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 75,000/-
b. Towards medical expenses Rs. 3,35,000/-

c. Towards loss of income during Rs. 66,000/-
laid up period d.
Towards disability Rs. 4,98,960/- e.

conveyance f.

Towards loss of amenities Rs. 45,000/- h.
Towards future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KP-7429.

Even though the respondent No.2 in its objection statement has denied the issuance of policy to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-04- KP-7429, no evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
23.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.10,95,960/- (Rupees Ten lakhs ninety five thousand nine hundred sixty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
